back: Used when the reporter is unimportant (e.g., 'Everyone was asked to bring food') [8].
Used to report what an unspecified group says (e.g., 'It is reported that damage is extensive') [8].
Verbs like allege, announce, believe, and report can be used in this pattern [8].
Alternative when the subject should be the topic (e.g., 'The damage is reported to be extensive') [8].
Most verbs from the it-pattern work, except announce, decide, mention, propose, recommend, suggest [8].
Used with discover, explain, find, etc. (e.g., 'It has now been revealed who was responsible') [8].
Used when a that-clause begins with 'there' (e.g., 'It is thought there are many obstacles' -> 'There are thought to be...') [8].

front: It was ... that Mrs Ho would chair the meeting.
It is ... that another moon landing will occur.

back: Patients have been reassured about hospital safety [9].
Water has been discovered on Mars [9].

front: Headline: POLICE TOLD TO WORK LONGER
back: Police have been told to work longer hours [9].

front: It has been ... that a fault caused the problem.
A mechanical fault was ... to have caused it.
